ambition.rationale:
Core problem, stated precisely: invert an elliptical, wind- and slope-driven fire-spread model against sparse, late, timed perimeters to recover where and when two real January 2025 fires started, with calibrated and identifiability-gated uncertainty. The repo adds matched-exposure house-level associations and a citation-checked LLM analyst on top. The LLM is the least ambitious part. The ambition sits in pipeline/ember/spread.py and pipeline/steps/s11_ignition.py, so this is not a familiar app with a model attached. Meta's models are not credited here; that belongs to the Meta bonus.

Hard, and not a wrapper: the back-trace is an in-house numerical search over ignition cell, start time and spread-rate scale (s11_ignition.py:171). Its uncertainty temperature is calibrated on half of the synthetic cases and checked on the other half (s11_ignition.py:351-352, 362). The benchmark perturbs the truth physics on purpose (s11_ignition.py:312), and a gate withholds the start time when the fit cannot pin it down (s11_ignition.py:239, 242). The difficulty is real: Eaton's start time is marked non-identifiable with a 15.5 h interval, Palisades hits the spread-rate ceiling, and Eaton's forward fit matches observed footprints at IoU 0.24-0.33.

Withheld on "wasn't possible a year ago": every method is established. The spread law is elliptical, with the length-to-breadth ratio cited to Anderson (1983) (spread.py:10, 143). The slope term is Rothermel-style (spread.py:6-7), arrival is a time-dependent Dijkstra (spread.py:12, 184), and the house-level statistics are Mantel-Haenszel and IRLS logistic (s09b_exposure.py:67, 91). The "why now" pitch (README.md:18) argues the inputs are public for January 2025 fires. It does not argue that a capability became possible in the last year, and no repo file dates source availability. The only 2026-specific element, Muse Spark tool calling (README.md:24), is a generic function-calling loop that has not run live (README.md:34). The physics that makes wildfire spread hard is scoped out: no spotting, and one wind point for the whole domain (spread.py:15-16, README.md:127). The README gives this as the reason Palisades fails (README.md:97).

Minor: the UI layout is copied from another concept (docs/spec/DESIGN.md:3). That is not the core problem, so it carries light weight. Drone segmentation and FIRMS are marked not started (README.md:36-37), so they are neither credited nor penalized here. The physics commit (e467f60) is dated 2026-10-30 03:07 PT, inside the window, so authorship timing does not change the score.

Net: a hard, candid, non-wrapper inverse problem built from classical methods, with no evidence of a capability that was impossible a year ago. 7 is the defensible score. 8 would need a new method or a new 2026 capability in the core.

depth.rationale: The repo is not a thin wrapper. Its hard part is hand-built: a numba time-dependent Dijkstra over an elliptical spread model, a candidate-search inversion with a hinge loss, a split-half calibrated uncertainty, an identifiability gate, Mantel-Haenszel and logistic statistics, stale-timestamp and placeholder detection in perimeter cleaning, and an analyst loop that checks citations against a server-side registry. The pipeline dependencies include no fire-model or statistics package, so the core is original code. Depth is held back because the physics is a simplified single-point-wind ellipse whose spread-rate scale k absorbs model error. The synthetic benchmark regenerates truth with the same spread function, so it is largely in-model. The Palisades fit (k=76.8) sits outside the benchmark's truth range and misses its own real hold-out. The guardrails are a keyword regex list. Share estimate, counting non-test code only (cmd: wc -l counts by directory): pipeline/ember 696, pipeline/steps 3961, pipeline/tools 395, web/api/_lib 1193, web/api/analyst.ts 108, web/scripts 373, web/src 1426, total 8152. My rough count of original algorithmic logic is spread.py 363, s11 about 430 of 525, s09b about 190 of 228, s06 about 200 of 263, s10 about 110 of 135, s05 rules about 400 of 615, analyst.ts 158, verify.ts 82, tools.ts about 370 of 617, eval-analyst.ts about 200 of 289, for about 2500, or roughly 30% of non-test code. The rest is data-fetch and reprojection glue plus the UI shell. Tests add 1683 lines that exercise the core. That is clearly above ordinary, but the depth is concentrated in roughly 900 lines of physics and inversion, and its real-data skill is mixed, so I stop short of 8.

Only planned: s12c_sam_video.py and s09c_sam_structures.py exit with "not implemented yet". The drone-footage and destroyed-building SAM work, and the SAM precision/recall eval, do not exist yet.

Not wired to the product: the Notes tab is a Pending placeholder. The analyst is reachable only through the API route and the CLI.

To reach 3, the repo needs a committed live smoke output for both models, a committed eval/analyst.json from a real run, and an offline test for the SAM request and parser path.

judge.rationale:
Verdict: reject. The fixed arithmetic gives 54.5 (weighted 52.5 + Meta bonus 2), below the 80 required by approval rule 1. Rule 2 passes: zero critical findings survived, and after checking the adversary's three major findings against the code I agree none is critical (numbers reproduce, failures are disclosed, the problems are overstatement). The 54.5 is depressed by two panel agents that failed rather than scored: works (20%) and execution (5%) both carry a 0 that is a harness failure, not a measurement. I re-scored both below; with my scores the total is about 67, so the gap to 80 is real (about 13 points), not an artifact of the failed agents.

What I verified myself, read-only (the sandbox classifier blocked me from executing the repo's test suite, so I could not run make test, npm test or npm run build; nobody ran those three this round). Code: s11_ignition.py constants and logic match every panel citation (FIT_HORIZON_H=48 at :53, K_GRID ceiling 64 at :55, K_TRUE_RANGE (4,16) at :57, 6 h gate at :62, search at :171, timing gate :233-242, the k prior chosen from the real Eaton fit :306-307, truth generated by the same sp.arrival with scaled parameters :310-316, split-half calibration :351-369, synthetic schedule anchored to CAL FIRE's start via ref_t :421, hold-out fit-only :444-477). spread.py is a hand-written numba time-dependent Dijkstra with a decrease-key heap, corner-cut guard, Anderson length-to-breadth ellipse and a hinge loss; pyproject.toml lists no fire-model or statistics package. Data, recomputed with my own script against the committed JSON: Eaton k=11.314, 6 of 10 perimeters used, start not identifiable (15.5 h); Palisades k=76.8 above the ceiling of 64, 5 of 11 used; at the calibrated tau 0 of 20 synthetic cases per fire pass the 6 h gate (minimum interval width 15.29 h Eaton, 15.27 h Palisades), so the headline start-time medians describe output the product never shows; Palisades calibration-half time coverage is 0.9 at all nine taus (tau 0.15 is the grid floor by default); Palisades hold-out is 2,821 min late and 2,750 m off, outside both 90% regions; Mantel-Haenszel ORs for vents, eaves and roof reproduce to three decimals from by_stratum for both fires; events.json has no ignition_estimate for either fire, matching the gate; arrival_meta.json seeds the first interval from CAL FIRE's start and location, and that seed interval holds 186,795 of 379,458 Palisades cells (49%), confirming adversary F9; manifest.json is 11 REAL / 6 MODELED. Adversary F1 (s11:421 uses ref_t for the calibration schedule), F2 (verify.ts:9-23 is a fixed regex list) and F3 (verify.ts:75 checks only cite-id membership in the registry, never content) are confirmed in the code. Web app: fire.ts:63-66 fetches only aoi, dem, manifest and final_perimeter; Stage.tsx:36 loads dem.png; nothing else in web/src fetches anything; Stage.tsx:50 renders syntheticArrival; Rail.tsx shows "pending · step 11" (:101), "Scaffold · data steps 1–2" (:115), "land in step 07" (:136) and two "lands Sunday" placeholders (:187, :189); Dock.tsx has no data source. So README:3 and README:100 ("what the app shows") describe a demo that does not exist yet, and report.py:99 hardcodes "Full fit (all perimeters)" into RESULTS.md:46 and :63 when the fit used 6 of 10 and 5 of 11. Those two are literal false statements; they are minor in effect but an adversary could classify them as "claim is false" next round, so they are must-fix, not polish. Tests: 77 pytest functions (parametrized over both fires; test_s11_ignition.py:22-34 runs a real inversion on the committed fixture) and 59 vitest cases against the README's "60"; every data file the tests reference exists for both fires. Git: 21 commits, author and committer dates equal, from Oct 29 21:35 to Oct 30 06:33 PT, inside the Oct 29 to Nov 4 window; five commits share the same second (03:42:52-53) and three share 03:24:33, so they were batch-split, and the final commit is a 195k-line output dump. A later commit on a/data (2d89006, 06:44) touches the calibration but is not the judged HEAD.

On the panel's substantive scores I agree with ambition 7, depth 7 and evidence 7, and with the Meta bonus of 2: the Muse Spark loop, verifier and eval harness are real and tested offline, but no live response from either model exists in the repo. My environment note for the next round: this machine defaults to Node 18 while web/ requires 20.19 (20.19.3 is installed under nvm), plain make eval runs 20 synthetic cases per fire, and make test includes a real inversion; any of these can sink an automated works agent, and the adversary's own successful runs of make eval QUICK=1 and npm run eval:analyst -- --truth show the offline path does work when the environment cooperates. The project is a serious, candid inverse-problem build; what it lacks for approval is a demo that shows its own outputs, a robust reproduce path, a live Meta run, and benchmark reporting that matches the gate it enforces.

disagreements.evidence: The panel's 0 is 'agent failed', not a measurement. Verified by the adversary's commands this round: make eval QUICK=1 runs for both fires from a clean checkout (fixture fallback at pipeline/steps/s11_ignition.py:85-105) and npm run eval:analyst -- --truth runs, so uv sync, numba and npm ci work. Unverified by anyone: make test, npm test, npm run build. Static checks: all data files the 77 pytest functions read exist for both fires; test_s11_ignition.py:22-34 runs a real inversion on the committed fixture; the back-trace runs on two fires, not one canned input. Withheld: the user-facing demo is a shell. web/src/data/fire.ts:63-66 loads only aoi, dem, manifest and final_perimeter; web/src/stage/Stage.tsx:50 renders syntheticArrival labelled SIM (overlays.tsx:54-63); web/src/rail/Rail.tsx:101, :115, :136, :187, :189 are placeholders; Dock.tsx charts have no data source; the analyst has never produced a live answer and its eval is hardcoded to Eaton (web/scripts/eval-analyst.ts:19). Likely causes of the harness failure visible in the files: Node 18 default vs engines >=20.19 (web/package.json:6-8, web/.nvmrc), plain make eval running 20 cases per fire (pipeline/Makefile:59-60, s11_ignition.py:402-403), and a slow inversion inside make test.

The panel's 0 is 'agent failed'. git log: 21 commits, author date == committer date on every one, from ab6e229 (2026-10-29 21:35 PT, design spec) to 23ee0c9 (2026-10-30 06:33 PT), all inside the hackathon window (docs/spec/BUILD.md:7-9: Thu Oct 29 night to Wed Nov 4 5 pm PST). Commit messages are per-step and coherent; the only prior work (Sentinel YOLOv8) is disclosed at README.md:164 and is not in the repo. Withheld: five commits share 03:42:52-53 (0b66b7f, 33c40c5, 5a8090f, 5df21c2, ba04683) and three share 03:24:33, so they were batch-split from one working tree and their timestamps do not show when the code was written; the history is a single 9 h burst by one author; the final commit is a 195k-line output dump. No evidence of pre-event code.

The rubric asks two things: does the README name the user, problem and why now (yes: README.md:9-24, with checkable numbers), and does the demo match it (no). README.md:3 promises street-level arrival, back-trace with uncertainty and matched-exposure comparison; README.md:100 says 'Full fit (what the app shows)'. The app loads none of these outputs: web/src/data/fire.ts:63-66 fetches four files, web/src/stage/Stage.tsx:36 loads dem.png, and no other fetch exists in web/src; Stage.tsx:50 draws a synthetic fire; Rail.tsx:101 shows 'pending · step 11', :115 'Scaffold · data steps 1–2', :187 and :189 'lands Sunday'; Dock.tsx:137-154 charts carry notes but no data. README.md:35 discloses the SIM layer, which keeps this at 6 rather than lower, but a judge who opens npm run dev sees a scaffold, not the pitch.
